text.p: Synalloy Corp said on Friday it is experiencing "unusual" cyclical weakness in both the metals and chemicals segments of its business since the second quarter of 1996.
Synalloy said its metals segment was hurt by a 28 percent decrease in prices for stainless steel pipe in the first quarter.
Synalloy increased its stainless steel pipe prices by eight percent on April 7, 1997, which could improve second quarter results if the price increase is accepted by the market, it said.
Synalloy said it rescinded a stainless steel pipe price increase in November 1996 after other producers did not raise prices.

In the chemicals segment, Textile dye and pigment demand continues to be weakend weak denim markets and continued softness in pigment demand from textile printers more than offset increased sales of other dyes, Synalloy said.

Chemical specialties, which were aided by the acquisition of Manufacturers Chemical in the last quarter of 1996, contributed 47 percent of the company's first quarter sales and a greater percentage of first quarter profits, Synalloy said.
Synalloy said it is poised to benefit from any recovery in the textile dye and pigment market and it will also continue to focus on its growing non-dye specialties.
